notApplicablePolicy: chartOwner and narrativeOwner use not-applicable for static reference routes; legacy means an actual compatibility producer remains.
loadingStrategyPolicy: fullNativeOwner requires route-dynamic-import in addition to native ownership (with only declared not-applicable dimensions), zero contested ids, and zero active legacy writer evidence.
method: Re-measured directly against the current working tree (bootstrap.js module wiring, router transition, async scope ownership, capability-level loading, cross-grep of native writer ids against js/*.js and index.html, including principles/masters/atlas route modules and their primary surface markers). Not copied from prior declarations.
rm01Note: CURRENT (A06, 2026-10-12): every one of the 19 active routes has rendererOwner=native; no route is legacy-rendered. chartOwner is native on 8 routes, legacy on 7 (home, signal, briefing, fundamental, theme-detail, market-news, screener) and not-applicable on 4 reference routes. dataOwner=native means the native reader/normalizer owns the value; some acquisition still fills legacy globals. HISTORICAL (kept as a ledger, not current state): RM-01 (2026-07-19) deleted every native setText/textContent write this file's contestedIds/legacyWriterEvidence originally documented as a live race (per RM-01 §2 default action: delete native, keep legacy). Those fields are kept as a historical DELETE-LEDGER record of what was found and removed, not a claim that the race is still live — for the 15 rendererOwner='legacy' routes, native no longer writes any of these ids at all. The real ARX cutover (deleting the *legacy* writer so native can take sole ownership) remains future per-route work; see route-owners.json openItems and the execution plan's ARX-05..11 packets.
rm05AgDomWriterProcedure: AG-DOM-WRITER (scripts/ci-architecture-contract-check.mjs) asserts the intersection of ids written by src/ui/{pages,components,knowledge}/**/*.js and ids written by every production js/aio-*.js (except aio-tests.js)+index.html is empty, except entries in domWriterIntersectionAllowlist below. Procedure for a real future route cutover (deleting the *legacy* writer so native takes sole ownership of a currently-legacy-owned id): (1) delete the legacy writer line(s) named in that route's legacyWriterEvidence array in this file; (2) re-add the native setText/textContent write for that id in the route's src/ui/pages/*.js module; (3) update that route's rendererOwner to 'native' and move its ids from contestedIds to a cleared state in this file; (4) if the id is also referenced by routeOwners.legacySymbolsMustBeAbsent for ANY renderer-native route (i.e. legacy code must never reintroduce a writer for it), add it there. Do NOT add a newly-cut-over id to domWriterIntersectionAllowlist — that list is exclusively for ids where legacy legitimately READS (not writes) a value native owns (see theme-detail-panel below), and an entry leaves once the id no longer intersects (v57.77 removed fg-score-big, pc-score-big and ticker-hero-name); an allowlist entry for a genuine two-way content race would defeat the gate's purpose.

columnDefinitions.lifecycleOwner: who mounts/disposes the route (native = ESM router transition owns it; PAGES[route].init is null)
columnDefinitions.rendererOwner: who owns the visible DOM content nodes for this route with no competing writer
columnDefinitions.dataOwner: who owns the fetch/normalize pipeline (native = independent of legacy.read* projection)
columnDefinitions.chartOwner: who owns chart/canvas instance lifecycle for this route
columnDefinitions.narrativeOwner: who generates the route's prose/summary text

masters.notes: Native SEC 13F reference route. It exposes 37 SEC filer profiles plus one separately labeled method-only educator, per-manager shards, filing/currentness discovery, reconciliation, holdings/change metrics, 2–4 manager comparison, official principles and explicit CURRENT/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/NOTICE states. SEC collection requires a policy-compliant repository SEC_USER_AGENT and never promotes discovery-only data.

atlas.notes: Native learner-first AI knowledge route with foundations, relationship, taxonomy and evidence views. Capability groups load by tab under route abort scope; search covers authored body/evidence; learning state and professional-route bridges are interactive. Structural role/product coverage stays separate from dated currentness and no unverified shipment, yield, valuation or trading claim is promoted.

guide.notes: No competing legacy _aioGuideSearchTrigger/_aioGuideJump function definitions found anywhere in js/*.js — genuinely uncontested. dataOwner is native because the route is served by the canonical runtime state boundary; chartOwner/narrativeOwner remain legacy only as not-applicable (static reference content, with no chart or generated narrative surface).

screener.notes: ARX-10/ARX-16: screener.js is the sole visible DOM owner and the native provider/orchestrator owns the canonical screener state and single artifact fetch. Non-route readers use AIO_ARCH.getScreenerRows() through the compatibility boundary; legacy profile/watchlist storage and identity/memo overlays remain as explicit compatibility producers.

RESOLVED (P1150): navigation now has a single transition authority. When the compatibility facade wraps `window.showPage`, it claims authority and the router's `aio:pageShown` listener becomes observation-only; the router publishes `aio:navigationCommitted` after a successful commit and bootstrap derives `store.route` from that event. A scalar page id is never read as an entity id, so one click = one scope transition with DOM/router/store in agreement (verified in ci-architecture-browser-check). Hosts without a writable `showPage` global retain the event path.
